newsitem.title: AZERBAIJAN: Azerbaijan to sign oil deal with Amoco, Unocal.
newsitem.headline: Azerbaijan to sign oil deal with Amoco, Unocal.

text.p: Azerbaijan will sign a $1.5 billion contract with an oil consortium including Amoco Corp. and Unocal Corp. next month to develop Caspian offshore reserves and is forging ahead with other deals, Azeri oil officials said Wednesday.

Spokesmen in the government and at Azeri state oil firm Socar said Chicago-based Amoco and Los Angeles-based Unocal, Itochu of Japan and Saudi Arabia's Delta Nimir would initial an agreement with Socar on Dec. 14 in the Azeri capital Baku to tap the Dan-Ulduzu and Azhrafe structures.
The fields are adjacent to the Karabakh structure in the Caspian's Apsheron ridge, in the Azeri sector of the sea.
The Socar source said Amoco would hold 30 percent, Unocal 25.5 percent, Itochu and Socar 20 percent each and Delta Nimir 4.5 percent. Unocal and Delta would work as an alliance.
Russia's Lukoil had shown interest in acquiring part of the Azeri stake but no agreements have yet been reached, the source said.
In a separate deal, Conoco has initialled a memorandum of understanding with Azeri officials on reserves in the Caspian's Gyuneshli structure not covered by another big contract.
Under the agreement, Conoco, a subsidiary of DuPont Co., may rehabilitate wells and drill new ones at Gyuneshli, which accounts for nearly three-quarters of Azeri oil output.
Azeri oil officials said Mobil Corp., Chevron Corp., Elf Aquitaine of France and Monument Oil and Gas Plc of Britain were among those also examining Caspian opportunities.
